Legendary graphic designer Susan Kare recently delivered a talk at the Startup School 2026 event, and the video of her speech has been uploaded to Y Combinator's YouTube channel. You can watch it below.

Susan Kare shared wonderful stories and design wisdom

It has been more than 40 years since the launch of the original Macintosh, yet the graphics, fonts, icons and overall UI elements of that system still look as eye-catching as they did back then.

In fact, many of the elements Susan Kare designed for the original Macintosh remain part of macOS to this day, both in spirit and in their original form. From the Command key symbol, the Happy Mac startup icon, the system font, to the hand-shaped cursor, Kare's work not only shaped the visual language of the Mac, but also influenced the entire personal computer industry.

Although anyone who has looked into Apple's history may have seen Kare's sketches, or even read or heard her interviews about that early work, hearing her personally recount the passion and frustrations—back when graphical user interfaces and bitmap images were still uncharted territory—is still very interesting.

Therefore, if you are interested in design, in Apple's history, or enjoy hearing someone share their lifelong passion from a professional perspective, Kare's talk is absolutely not to be missed.

In addition to detailing her work at Apple, Kare also talked about how she joined the company, showcased her work after leaving, shared some early Apple anecdotes, and quoted other legendary designers, bringing extra inspiration to the audience.
